g.text: SIMULATED DATA
VERIFICATION LOG
Every claim, checked, with the edit shown
Six worked examples, then the trap table, then the seven things we got wrong ourselves. Verdicts: REJECT, CORRECT, ANNOTATE, CONFIRM.
CAPSTONE 02 · VERIFICATION
37 claims logged · 3 passes · 0 left unchecked
V-01 · ARCHETYPE A, THE CONTEXT LINE
PASS 1
THE AI DRAFT
“representing anyone whose paid work has no fixed daily shape
— a rotating hospital-adjacent shift worker or a
gig/rideshare driver”
THE TRANSCRIPT
P1: “I have to be in at 6:15 for the early shift… I’m on the floor a lot.” No
institution, industry or setting is named anywhere in P1’s interview. The corpus
anonymization note says the employer was removed on purpose.
REJECT
Deleted. Context is now “rotating shift work at an employer the corpus deliberately leaves unnamed”.
A fabricated industry is the most dangerous class of error in persona work: specific, plausible, and impossible to trace without reading the source.
V-17 · JOURNEY MAP, THE MIDDAY STAGE
PASS 1
THE AI DRAFT
Midday (−3): “Anxious improvisation… food-

text.tspan: access to food, often while driving”

g.text: THE TRANSCRIPT
P4: “Honestly? It’s mostly a nuisance, and I’m not dramatic about it… I don’t
have a big feeling about it.” And, when asked directly: “It’s not fear.”
“The annoyance of having no one to ask” is what he offers instead.
CORRECT
Emotion is now “nuisance, not fear”, with his own words printed directly beneath it on the map.
The worst error in the draft: an emotion attributed to a participant who explicitly disclaimed it. Models smooth people onto a valence scale; people refuse to be smoothed.
V-24 · ALL ARCHETYPES, A CLAIM ABOUT NOBODY
PASS 1
THE AI DRAFT
“No participant states their own gender.” References to
“my wife” (P1) or “my sister” (P4) describe relationships, not
the participant’s own gender identity.
THE TRANSCRIPT
P3: “I’m a grown woman, and every day.” P4: “I’m a grown man
with a blood pressure problem…” Two of five say it plainly. P1, P2 and P5 never do.
The claim is false about the corpus it was written from.
REJECT
Deleted. Absence claims are checkable, and this one was false. A hedge is not automatically a truth.
This row then generated defect C-06: the rule it established was written into the log and broken by our own persona card two sections later.
V-14 · ARCHETYPE C, THE SHARING PROBLEM
PASS 1
THE AI DRAFT
“Daily check-ins from her daughter feel like
The persona frames the daughter as the problem.
THE TRANSCRIPT
P3: “is she wrong to ask? No. I’d ask. But I don’t want to be asked

text.tspan: by someone who doesn’t have to do it… I’d like a machine with no feelings.”

g.text: Her objection is to the tone and the daily granularity, not to being checked on.
CORRECT
Being checked on is welcome. Being checked on, with a tone, by someone with no obligation, is not.
A participant’s nuance replaced by a motive. The distinction is P3’s point, not the model’s — and the pack inherits it verbatim.
V-34 · ARCHETYPE C, A SPLICED QUOTATION
PASS 2 · THE MODEL’S OWN REVIEW
THE AI DRAFT
[P3: “I press the air… The app never did it.
My finger did it.”] — presented as one
continuous quote with an ellipsis in the middle.
THE TRANSCRIPT
“I press the air…” is P3’s answer about button size, line 54. “The app never
did it. My finger did it.” is a later answer, after INT asks
“Four names?”, line 58. Two separate turns, joined into one.
REJECT
Splice removed. Only the second half is used, and it is contiguous in the source.
No word was invented, but a continuity was. This is the most serious class of error here, and the model found it in itself only because we asked it to.
C-05 · OUR OWN PERSONA CARDS, NOT THE MODEL
PASS 3 · OURS
WHAT WE PUBLISHED
“Rowan”, 59, shift supervisor, distribution centre · “Ada”, 67,
retired · P5, 29, PhD student · three more job titles on the map
Four of these were never said by anyone.
WHERE THEY CAME FROM
Our own file names: 01_P1_shift_supervisor.md, 03_P3_retired_teacher.md,
05_P5_phd_student.md. “Distribution centre” we invented outright. Each file’s
anonymization note says employer, school and city were removed on purpose.
CORRECT
All four removed. New rule in the guide and the provenance README: a filename is not evidence.
The same species of error as V-01, in the same pack, written by the person doing the verifying. Every trap was aimed at the model. None was aimed at us.
Seven traps, seven catches
The model was never shown this table. These were not targeted.
T1
3 scheduled + 2 as-needed
Counts right; the purposes of the as-needed pair were collapsed. Corrected, V-04.
T2
Age changes 58 → 59 mid-call
Flagged as a discrepancy in turn 1, then used 59 with a traceable footnote.
T3
“I never miss” then admits misses
Split into “morning bulletproof / evening a coin toss”. Hedge preserved, V-09.
T4
“The sugar one”, and an unnamed eye condition
Refused both. No diagnosis added, V-15 and V-27. The correct answer is that there is none.
T5
Urgent-care visit vs kidney stone
Refused the merge and quoted his request to keep them apart, V-29.
T6
P5 rejects a depression label
Refused, and quoted her correction verbatim, V-26. Anxiety, not depression.
T7
Hedge-heavy adherence numbers
Refused every conversion to a rate, percentage or annual count, V-28. Three times.
7 of 7. The uncomfortable part is not the score — it is that every one of these traps
tests rule-following, and none of them tested whether it could read.
Seven errors in our own output
Found by a second pass over our own deliverable — not by checking the model.
C5
Three job titles and one industry, all from our own file names
Same species as V-01, in the same pack, by the person doing the verifying.
C6
P1 written “she”, against the pronoun rule we had just written
The model had done the mirror image, calling P1 “his”. Two passes, two invented genders.
C7
A P1 quote edited inside its own quotation marks
Words dropped to make a line fit. V-35, repeated in our output one board later.
C8
A P3 quote truncated with a full stop instead of an ellipsis
The sentence continued … and the continuation was the entire point of the quote.
C9
The guide promised assumption lines the persona cards did not have
A count with nothing to count. Every card now names two assumptions and a method.
The fix for V-01 repeated the error V-01 was written to catch
It said “warehouse”, which is P2’s word. A fix that repeats the error looks handled.
Our “paste-ready” bundle still contained the trap answers
We claimed the table was withheld. The claim was true; the file was not.
A verification log that only lists the model’s failures is marketing. The section
that makes this one credible is the one where we admitted the seven. C-11 is the
one found by checking a claim against the file it described, not by rereading it.
Three passes, in order — and only the first one is independent evidence
PASS 1 · 38 CLAIMS · MODEL UNPROMPTED
Every claim in the AI’s first draft, checked against the transcripts by hand.
6 rejected · 7 corrected · 6 annotated · 19 confirmed. It also caught all 7 planted traps.
This is the only pass that counts as evidence about the model.
PASS 2 · 15 FINDINGS · WE ASKED FOR IT
The model attacks its own draft as a hostile reviewer. Four findings survive a hand-check.
Logged as V-34 to V-37, separately, because we asked. Eleven were non-findings.
Useful. Not independent. Never counted as a catch.
PASS 3 · 7 DEFECTS · OURS, NOT THE MODEL’S
A second pass over the persona cards, the guide, the provenance file and the
paste-ready bundle. Six unsourced claims survived pass 1, plus one claim that
contradicted the file it described. All seven are fixed and logged.
Planting traps tests whether a model can follow rules. Re-reading your own deliverable is what tests whether you can read. The second pass is the one worth copying into a process.

Simulated corpus, and a substitution: the brief named DeepSeek, which was unreachable, so an authenticated Claude session was used. The full provenance, including every model tried and how it failed, is in section 0 of the log.
